# `gh-tmpl issue create`

- **Usage:** `gh-tmpl issue create [FLAGS] [gh_args]…`

Check the body against the issue template, then run "gh issue create".

gh-tmpl reads the body from --body, -b, --body-file or -F, checks it, and
stops with exit code 1 if the check fails. If the body passes, it runs
"gh issue create" with every argument except the --tmpl-* flags. Without
--body or --body-file there is no body to check, so it runs gh directly.

## Arguments
- **`[gh_args]…`** — Arguments for gh issue create, passed on in order

## Flags
- **`--tmpl-name <template>`** — Check against the template with this ID or name
- **`--tmpl-strict`** — Fail on warnings too
- **`--tmpl-allow-unchecked`** — Report an untouched checklist as a warning, not an error
- **`--tmpl-offline`** — Do not read the owner's shared .github repository
- **`--tmpl-skip`** — Run gh without the check

## Examples

```
gh tmpl issue create --tmpl-name bug_report --title "Crash" --body-file body.md
```
